articles.headline: NBA Rank 2026: The new top 10 features a razor-thin race for No. 1
articles.description: Our countdown of the NBA's top 100 players hits its grand finale.
articles.body:
Welcome to the grand finale of NBA Rank 2026.

After unveiling Nos. 100-51 on Tuesday and Nos. 50-11 on Wednesday, the big reveal is here.

Who will be the top 10 players for the 2026-27 season? How high did reigning Finals MVP Jalen Brunson climb? Did Victor Wembanyama just begin a LeBron James-esque run atop of the list?

While ESPN's latest top 10 -- er, full top 100 -- will surely spark debate, what can't be questioned is the remarkably tight race for this season's No. 1 spot. Just three voting points separated Nikola Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Wembanyama, with each superstar placing atop at least one of the seven panelists' individual rankings.

That panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition. In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list.

That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven NBA experts: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list -- the best of the best heading into the new NBA season.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

10. Donovan Mitchell

G | Cleveland Cavaliers

Age: 30

2025 NBA Rank: 15

Mitchell rises into the top 10 after leading the Cavaliers to the Eastern Conference finals last season, his first such appearance in his nine-year career. He has finished in the top seven in MVP voting in three of the past four seasons, and his ability to create off the dribble while using his shooting range to freeze defenders makes him the offensive force of the Cavs. Mitchell has been an All-Star in seven straight seasons, and he pairs with James Harden to give Cleveland one of the few backcourts where each starter boasts multiple All-NBA selections. 

Biggest question: Can Mitchell be the best player on a champion?

The Cavaliers start four All-Stars in Mitchell, Harden, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, but in the playoffs they will go only as far as Mitchell can lead them.

One of the ironies of Mitchell's first run to the conference finals was that he didn't play particularly well compared with past postseasons. In his six playoffs runs, from 2020 to 2025, Mitchell averaged 30.0 points per game with a player efficiency rating of 24.5. Last season, he averaged 26.0 points with a PER of just 18.6 (15.0 is considered average). The former version is absolutely good enough to carry the Cavs back to the Finals, especially if Mitchell sees a repeat performance from his teammates. -- André Snellings

Signature stat: Mitchell is one of eight players to average at least 20 points per game in each

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Bayern's Karl to get 'dream' Real Madrid move?
articles.description: Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl could get his dream move to Real Madrid. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl could get his dream move to Real Madrid, while AC Milan are planning to sign USMNT winger Christian Pulisic to a new contract. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are keeping tabs on Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl, according to Bild's Christian Falk. Los Blancos are among several teams interested in the 18-year-old, with whom the Bundesliga champions plan to open contract renewal talks, while rival clubs monitor whether Michael Olise's presence in his position could create a transfer opportunity. Karl said during an event in January that playing for Madrid would be a "dream" which led to an apology after the comments sparked anger among Bayern fans.

- AC Milan are planning to sign USMNT winger Christian Pulisic to a new contract extending until the summer of 2031, according to Corriere dello Sport. Initial talks have begun with the 28-year-old's representatives over a deal worth around €5 million per season following his goal-scoring performance in Sunday's 3-0 win over Lecce.

- Chelsea are considering Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton and Feyenoord's Gjivai Zechiël as potential successors to Enzo Fernández, TEAMtalk reports. The 22-year-old Zechiel has registered five goals and four assists in seven Eredivisie matches this season, attracting interest from Chelsea, Liverpool, and five other Premier League clubs.

- Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri is being scouted by Juventus, according to Gazzetta dello Sport. The 25-year-old tops the Bianconeri shortlist for the January transfer window, with a loan approach lined up due to his lack of playing time under Enzo Maresca, while RB Leipzig's David Raum is considered an alternative.

- Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa are interested in Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae, according to Christian Falk. Both clubs have tracked the 29-year-old South Korea international since the summer, though any move is expected to depend on upcoming contract discussions with the German club.

Other rumors

- Arsenal are among four Premier League teams tracking Sturm Graz midfielder Luca Weinhandl, 17. (TEAMtalk)

- Barcelona sent scouts to watch Athletico Paranaense defender Arthur Dias in their 2-1 victory over Bahia on Sunday. (Sport)

- Bayern Munich are not considering a move for Newcastle United striker Nick Woltemade, who is currently on loan at Juventus, despite recent reports. (Christian Falk)

- Liverpool, Arsenal, and Chelsea are among the clubs tracking Real Sociedad defender Jon Martín. (Ekrem Konur)

- Aston Villa are preparing contract extension talks with attacking midfielder Emiliano Buendía. (Daily Mail)

- Roma and AC Milan are lining up a loan approach for Real Madrid striker Endrick in January. (Calciomercato)

articles.headline: NBA Rank 2026 audit: What we got right -- and wrong -- in our top 100
articles.description: Using an analytical lens, Dean Oliver examines what the NBA Rank panel got right -- and what it got very wrong.
articles.body:
When combing through ESPN's latest countdown of the top 100 NBA players, try to remember one phrase, which is just as applicable to ranking players as it is to building a winning roster.

People see the game better than numbers, but numbers see all the games.

As it relates to NBA Rank 2026, those numbers are a collective of advanced player ratings commonly in use, from ESPN's Net Points to DARKO, LEBRON, EPM and RAPM. Those systems can provide a useful counter perspective to the humans, with their good eyes but occasional biases.

With the full top 100 unveiled for the 2026-27 season, let's examine what the metrics revealed about which player rankings our panelists got right -- and which they got wrong.

Four things NBA Rank got wrong

1. Jalen Brunson (No. 6)

Our last view of Brunson is him carrying the Knicks to a fourth-quarter comeback in Game 5 of the NBA Finals. He was tremendous in New York's run to the championship -- but that leads to the bias that he will maintain it.

He was Finals MVP, but will he really finish the season as the league's sixth-best player? Brunson has always been limited a bit by his size (6-foot-2, 190 pounds) and his defense, something the metrics perhaps see and remember more than the seven panelists remember the late buckets he poured in to win the Finals. Those problems are likely to persist.

I love Brunson's game, but his lofty ranking benefitted not only from recent bias but also from the New York media bias. (That bias might also help you forget that Brunson missed the shot in the most iconic image from the Finals, when OG Anunoby swooped in for the putback game-winner to clinch Game 4.)

The metrics place Brunson around the No. 25 range heading into the season. That's not a huge gap. He's elite, just not No. 6 -- at least not during the regular season.

2. Rookies

Another bias comes from wanting to believe the hype. AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson, Cameron Boozer and Caleb Wilson all make the top 100, but rookies are generally bad NBA players -- predraft highlights don't show the turnovers, or the missed boxouts, or the poor defense.

Is it possible one or two rookies end the year in the top 100 of Net Points per game, per 100 possessions, or another metric? Of course. It's a strong draft, but history suggests these rankings could be a year too early.

3. Jaylen Brown (No. 14)

Without the rehabbing Jayson Tatum, the Celtics were picked to win about 40 games last year, so their overperformance led to a Coach of the Year award for Joe Mazzulla and to a shower of praise for Brown.

The claims of Brown being the league's "best two-way player" came mostly after he had his best game of the year against the LA Clippers and Kawhi Leonard, but few noticed Brown's next game, where he scored 14 points on 24 field goal attempts. Maybe we term this a "highlight bias" because our voters perhaps saw those highlights and loved him, ranking Brown between No. 9 and No. 23. The metrics' average, meanwhile, was around No. 60.
